+using System.ComponentModel;
+using ModelContextProtocol.Server;
+
+namespace McpHttpServer;
+
+/// <summary>
+/// Exposes application configuration as an MCP resource.
+/// </summary>
+[McpServerResourceType]
+public sealed class ConfigResourceProvider
+{
+    private static readonly Dictionary<string, string> Settings = new()
+    {
+        ["app.name"] = "McpHttpServer",
+        ["app.version"] = "1.0.0",
+        ["app.environment"] = "Development",
+        ["feature.logging"] = "true",
+        ["feature.metrics"] = "true",
+    };
+
+    [McpServerResource(
+        UriTemplate = "config://settings",
+        Name = "Application Settings",
+        Description = "Returns all application configuration settings as JSON")]
+    public static string GetAllSettings()
+    {
+        return System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(Settings, new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions
+        {
+            WriteIndented = true
+        });
+    }
+
+    [McpServerResource(
+        UriTemplate = "config://settings/{key}",
+        Name = "Setting by Key",
+        Description = "Returns a single configuration value by key")]
+    public static string GetSetting(string key)
+    {
+        return Settings.TryGetValue(key, out var value)
+            ? value
+            : throw new KeyNotFoundException($"Setting '{key}' not found.");
+    }
+}

Here's the working MCP HTTP server in `McpHttpServer/`:

**Key setup points:**

1. **`Program.cs`** — Register MCP with `.AddMcpServer().WithHttpTransport()`, then map the endpoint with `app.MapMcp()`. Use `.WithToolsFromAssembly()` to auto-discover tools and `.WithResources<T>()` to register resource providers.

2. **`ConfigResourceProvider.cs`** — Mark the class with `[McpServerResourceType]` and methods with `[McpServerResource]`. Use `UriTemplate` for the resource URI. Templates with `{key}` become parameterized resources. Descriptions go on a separate `[Description]` attribute (not a property of `McpServerResource`).

3. **`EchoTool.cs`** — Standard `[McpServerToolType]` / `[McpServerTool]` pattern for tools.

**Verified working** — the server responds to MCP Streamable HTTP requests at the root path, listing both the `echo` tool and `config://settings` resource, and returning config JSON when reading the resource.
